dedup.scope: Same-source public primary and all five claims already prepared from this source, plus the public identity index, the retired-claims record and the current worklist searched with the object names thin set, uniformly computable colouring, dominating modulus, k-th Turing jump, rainbow and Schreier barrier.

compared.difference: Same source but a different unit: that public item counts the proposition printed at source lines 585-587, which in this fixed v3 source lies inside the authors' iffalse block at 584-626 and is therefore no longer part of the paper; its content is a Weihrauch and Reverse-Mathematics reduction between the exactly-omega-large free set and rainbow principles, not a computability-theoretic construction of uniform colourings.

Counts Theorem ts-omega-computes-omega-jump (source lines 719-721), the single exactly-omega-large thin colouring whose thin sets compute the omega-th jump. lem:arrays is the uniformly indexed finite-dimensional ingredient proved immediately before it (lines 683-697); that theorem is not a premise here, and the uniformity in n and k is exactly what it later consumes.

Counts Theorem fs_red_rt (source lines 419-421), the strong Weihrauch reduction of the exactly-omega-large free set theorem to binary Ramsey; different section, different objects, and no Turing-jump coding.

Counts the computable progressive-barrier halting-code proposition (source lines 1057-1059), a barrier and forcing construction; it never uses a modulus of the k-th jump or thin sets of n-element tuples.

Counts the strong cone avoidance theorem (source lines 1083-1089); cone avoidance asserts that solutions avoid a cone, the opposite direction from the jump-coding conclusion proved here, and its machinery is not used.
Counts the two-bounded-rainbow halting-code proposition for barriers of order type omega to the omega (source lines 905-907); different principle, different construction.

compared.difference: Near neighbours returned were 199793 (arxiv:2605.03523:thm:fs_red_rt, free sets, thin sets and rainbows for barriers), 208568 (arxiv:2608.25339:thm:equivalence, thin set theorem for arbitrarily many colours implies bounding), 205589 (arxiv:2607.17666:lemma, Hindman's theorem does not code the omega-th jump in one application) and 192342 (arxiv:2601.05442:lem-solns-zn, arithmetic rainbow Ramsey multiplicities). None of them constructs a uniformly computable array of thin colourings whose thin sets compute the k-th jump.
